# GICHighDimension

GICHighDimension addresses the computational barrier of solving
$`\ell_0`$-penalized regression in linear models where the number of
predictors $`p`$ is large, in the hundreds or even the thousands, yet
smaller than the number of observations $`n`$. Finding the optimal
solution of $`\ell_0`$-penalized regression has been treated as a
combinatorial problem that requires discrete optimization and is
NP-hard. This package builds on a connection with Hopfield networks,
which are used for associative memory retrieval ([Xiao and Walker,
2026](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11222-026-10853-5)). It makes generalized
information criteria (GIC; [Kim, Kwon and Choi,
2012](https://jmlr.org/papers/v13/kim12a.html)) for variable selection,
which are equivalent to $`\ell_0`$-penalized regression, computationally
feasible. The rationale is that there remains strong interest in GIC,
whose statistical properties are superior to those of $`\ell_1`$-based
regularization.

A model with $`d`$ selected predictors scores
$`\mathrm{GIC}_d = y^\top H_d y / n - p(n, d)`$, where $`H_d`$ is its
hat matrix and the penalty $`p(n, d)`$ depends on the criterion. Table 1
of Xiao and Walker (2026) lists some criteria in the class of GIC:

| Name | $`p(n, d)`$ | Reference |
|:---|:---|:---|
| GIC2 | $`d \, \frac{\sigma^2}{n} \, d^{1/3}`$ | [Kim et al. (2012)](https://jmlr.org/papers/v13/kim12a.html) |
| GIC3 | $`2d \, \frac{\sigma^2}{n} \log d`$ | [Kim et al. (2012)](https://jmlr.org/papers/v13/kim12a.html) |
| GIC4 | $`2d \, \frac{\sigma^2}{n} (\log d + \log\log d)`$ | [Kim et al. (2012)](https://jmlr.org/papers/v13/kim12a.html) |
| GIC5 | $`d \, \frac{\sigma^2}{n} \log\log n \, \log d`$ | [Kim et al. (2012)](https://jmlr.org/papers/v13/kim12a.html) |
| GIC6 | $`d \, \frac{\sigma^2}{n} \log n \, \log d`$ | [Kim et al. (2012)](https://jmlr.org/papers/v13/kim12a.html) |
| CAIC | $`d \, \frac{\sigma^2}{n} (\log n + 1)`$ | [Bozdogan (1987)](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02294361) |
| SIC | $`d \, \frac{\sigma^2}{n} \sqrt{n}`$ | Shao (1997) |

The examples below highlight some well-known statistical properties of
these criteria:

1.  In linear regression, AIC is minimax-rate optimal and BIC is
    consistent. In the linear-model figure, AIC (blue line) attains the
    largest criterion value at the expense of many false positives.
2.  Criteria in the GIC family achieve consistency at different rates.
    GIC6 (green line) reaches the true model within two passes of the
    search, while BIC (orange line) still includes noise variables at
    the end.
3.  Consistency is an asymptotic result. Doubling the sample size
    (dotted lines) is not yet enough for BIC: with 500 candidate
    predictors, it still adds a few noise variables at $`n = 2000`$ and
    needs a much larger sample to select the true model.

## Installation

Install the development version of `GICHighDimension` from GitHub:

``` r

devtools::install_github("yuchenxiao95/GICHighDimension")
```

You also need Julia (≥ 1.9), which you can download from
<https://julialang.org/downloads/>. Then connect R to Julia; the first
time, also install the Julia packages the package uses:

``` r

library(GICHighDimension)
setup_julia()
install_julia_packages()   # first time only
```

## Examples

The examples below compare three criteria on the same data. In
increasing order of penalty per variable, they are AIC ($`c_n = 1`$),
BIC ($`\log n`$) and GIC6 ($`\log n \, \log P`$), where $`P`$ is the
number of candidate predictors. The [Examples
article](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/articles/examples.html)
([`vignette("examples")`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/articles/examples.md))
explains each step, and the Get started article
([`vignette("get-started")`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/articles/get-started.md))
lists all criteria and response families.

Helper functions used in the examples

``` r

set_seeds <- function(seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  JuliaCall::julia_command(sprintf("import Random; Random.seed!(%d);", seed))
}

criteria <- c(AIC = "Calculate_AIC", BIC = "Calculate_BIC", GIC6 = "Calculate_GIC6")
sample_sizes <- c(n1000 = 1000, n2000 = 2000)

# Run the search once per criterion, on the first n observations for each n
compare_criteria <- function(X, Y, init, k, Nsim) {
  lapply(sample_sizes, function(n) {
    Xn <- X[1:n, ]
    Yn <- if (is.matrix(Y)) Y[1:n, , drop = FALSE] else Y[1:n]
    lapply(criteria, function(crit)
      GICSelection(Xn, Yn, init, crit, paste0(crit, "_short"), k = k, Nsim = Nsim))
  })
}

last_model <- function(fit) sort(fit$selected_coeffs[[length(fit$selected_coeffs)]])

# Size, false positives and false negatives of each final model
selection_table <- function(fits, truth) {
  rows <- lapply(fits, function(by_crit) t(sapply(by_crit, function(fit) {
    s <- last_model(fit)
    c(size = length(s), false_pos = length(setdiff(s, truth)),
      false_neg = length(setdiff(truth, s)))
  })))
  out <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  rownames(out) <- paste(rep(names(fits), each = length(criteria)), rownames(out))
  out
}
```

Each figure shows, for every criterion, its value and the number of
selected variables after each search step: solid lines for $`n = 1000`$
and dotted lines for $`n = 2000`$. Light grey vertical lines mark a new
pass over the predictors, and the dashed line marks the true model size.
Criteria with larger penalties take lower values, so compare the shapes
of the curves, not their heights. The script
[`data-raw/readme_figures.R`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/data-raw/readme_figures.R)
runs the code in this section and redraws the figures.

All examples use the same setting. The design matrix $`X`$ has
$`n = 2000`$ observations of $`p = 500`$ independent standard normal
predictors, so the predictor covariance is $`\Sigma = I`$, and only a
few predictors affect the response. Every search runs twice, on the
first 1000 observations and on all 2000.

### Linear model

Here the response is $`Y = X\beta + \varepsilon`$ with
$`\varepsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I)`$. Five randomly chosen coefficients
equal 2 and the rest are 0, and $`\sigma^2`$ gives a signal-to-noise
ratio of $`\beta^\top\Sigma\beta/\sigma^2 = 0.71`$. Every search starts
from the full model:

``` r

set_seeds(1)
n <- 2000; p <- 500
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)
true_cols <- sort(sample(p, 5))
beta <- numeric(p); beta[true_cols] <- 2
Y <- LP_to_Y(X, beta, family = "Normal", std = sqrt(sum(beta^2) / 0.71))

fits <- compare_criteria(X, Y, 1:p, k = p, Nsim = 5)
selection_table(fits, true_cols)
#>            size false_pos false_neg
#> n1000 AIC   230       225         0
#> n1000 BIC     8         3         0
#> n1000 GIC6    5         0         0
#> n2000 AIC   197       192         0
#> n2000 BIC     9         4         0
#> n2000 GIC6    5         0         0
```

![Criteria and model size along the search, linear model with p =
500](reference/figures/README-linear.png)

Criteria and model size along the search, linear model with p = 500

GIC6 selects exactly the 5 true predictors at both sample sizes. BIC
keeps all 5 but adds 3 noise variables at $`n = 1000`$ and 4 at
$`n = 2000`$: doubling $`n`$ does not help, because its penalty ignores
the 500 candidates. AIC keeps about 200 variables at either size.

### Multivariate normal

Five responses, each with its own 5 predictors and coefficients from 10
down to 0.1. Pass the $`n \times 5`$ response matrix as `Y`:

``` r

m <- 5
B <- matrix(0, p, m)
true_by_response <- vector("list", m)
for (i in 1:m) {
  cols <- sort(sample(p, 5))
  true_by_response[[i]] <- cols
  B[cols, i] <- seq(10, 0.1, length.out = 5)
}
Y_multi <- LP_to_Y(X, B, family = "MultivariateNormal", cov_matrix = diag(m))
true_union <- sort(unique(unlist(true_by_response)))

fits <- compare_criteria(X, Y_multi, 1:p, k = p, Nsim = 5)
selection_table(fits, true_union)
#>            size false_pos false_neg
#> n1000 AIC   268       245         1
#> n1000 BIC    20         0         4
#> n1000 GIC6   19         0         5
#> n2000 AIC   232       208         0
#> n2000 BIC    20         0         4
#> n2000 GIC6   19         0         5
```

![Criteria and model size along the search, multivariate normal
response](reference/figures/README-multivariate.png)

Criteria and model size along the search, multivariate normal response

Two responses share a predictor, so 24 predictors are truly active. BIC
and GIC6 select no noise variables at either sample size. Every
predictor they miss (4 for BIC, 5 for GIC6) has a coefficient of 0.1,
which is too small to detect with 1000 or 2000 observations. AIC finds
all 24 at $`n = 2000`$, but inside a model of 232 variables.

### Generalized linear models

For a non-Gaussian response, map it to the linear-predictor scale with
[`Y_to_LP()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/Y_to_LP.md),
select with
[`GICSelection()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/GICSelection.md),
and then fit the selected model with
[`Beta_estimate()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/Beta_estimate.md).
The GLM examples reuse the design matrix `X` from above ($`n = 2000`$,
$`p = 500`$), with 5 true predictors, and start each search from the
first 10 columns.

``` r

set_seeds(2)
true_cols <- c(3, 17, 42, 88, 150)
beta <- numeric(p); beta[true_cols] <- c(1, -1, 0.8, -0.8, 0.6)

compare_glm <- function(Y, ...) compare_criteria(X, Y_to_LP(Y, ...), 1:10, k = 50, Nsim = 3)
```

#### Poisson regression

``` r

y_pois <- LP_to_Y(X, beta, family = "Poisson")
fits <- compare_glm(y_pois, family = "Poisson")
selection_table(fits, true_cols)
#>            size false_pos false_neg
#> n1000 AIC    49        45         1
#> n1000 BIC     9         4         0
#> n1000 GIC6    5         0         0
#> n2000 AIC    49        45         1
#> n2000 BIC    10         5         0
#> n2000 GIC6    5         0         0

# Coefficients of the GIC6 model for n = 2000, intercept first
round(Beta_estimate(X[, last_model(fits$n2000$GIC6)], y_pois, family = "Poisson"), 2)
#> [1] -0.03  1.00 -1.01  0.79 -0.80  0.62
```

![Criteria and model size along the search, Poisson
response](reference/figures/README-poisson.png)

Criteria and model size along the search, Poisson response

#### Binomial counts (10 trials)

``` r

y_binom <- LP_to_Y(X, beta, family = "Binomial", n_trials = 10)
fits <- compare_glm(y_binom, family = "Binomial", n_trials = 10)
selection_table(fits, true_cols)
#>            size false_pos false_neg
#> n1000 AIC    49        47         3
#> n1000 BIC     9         4         0
#> n1000 GIC6    5         0         0
#> n2000 AIC    49        46         2
#> n2000 BIC     8         3         0
#> n2000 GIC6    5         0         0
```

![Criteria and model size along the search, binomial
response](reference/figures/README-binomial.png)

Criteria and model size along the search, binomial response

#### Multinomial (three categories)

The coefficients form a $`p \times 2`$ matrix, and category 3 is the
baseline:

``` r

B_mn <- matrix(0, p, 2)
B_mn[true_cols, 1] <- 1.5
B_mn[true_cols, 2] <- c(-1.5, 1.5, -1.5, 1.5, -1.5)
y_mn <- LP_to_Y(X, B_mn, family = "Multinomial", n_categories = 3)
fits <- compare_glm(y_mn, family = "Multinomial", n_categories = 3)
selection_table(fits, true_cols)
#>            size false_pos false_neg
#> n1000 AIC    49        47         3
#> n1000 BIC     9         4         0
#> n1000 GIC6    5         0         0
#> n2000 AIC    49        48         4
#> n2000 BIC     8         3         0
#> n2000 GIC6    5         0         0
```

![Criteria and model size along the search, multinomial
response](reference/figures/README-multinomial.png)

Criteria and model size along the search, multinomial response

In all three GLMs, GIC6 selects exactly the 5 true predictors at both
sample sizes. BIC keeps the true predictors but adds 3 to 5 noise
variables, with no clear gain from doubling $`n`$. AIC grows the model
until it hits the size cap (`k = 50`, so at most 49 variables) and
misses 1 to 4 true predictors.

# Package index

## Variable selection

Search over variable subsets to maximize an information criterion. This
is how you will usually use the package.

- [`GICSelection()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/GICSelection.md)
  : GIC-Based Variable Selection
- [`GICSelectionBoltzmann()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/GICSelectionBoltzmann.md)
  : GIC-Based Variable Selection Using Boltzmann Machine

## Information criteria

AIC, BIC, EBIC, GIC2–GIC6 and related criteria. Pass the name of a
criterion (and of its `_short` version) to
[`GICSelection()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/GICSelection.md),
or call these functions directly to score a single model.

- [`Calculate_AIC()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_AICc()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_AttIC()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_SIC()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_BIC()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_CAIC()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_CAICF()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_EBIC()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_GIC2()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_GIC3()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_GIC4()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_GIC5()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_GIC6()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_AIC_Short()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_AICc_Short()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_AttIC_Short()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_SIC_Short()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_BIC_Short()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_CAIC_Short()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_CAICF_Short()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_EBIC_Short()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_GIC2_Short()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_GIC3_Short()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_GIC4_Short()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_GIC5_Short()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  [`Calculate_GIC6_Short()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/information_criteria.md)
  : Information Criterion Calculations via Julia

## Simulation and link transforms

Simulate responses from a linear predictor, map responses to the
linear-predictor scale, and generate sparse coefficient vectors. All
common GLM families are supported.

- [`LP_to_Y()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/LP_to_Y.md)
  : Transform Linear Predictor to Response
- [`Y_to_LP()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/Y_to_LP.md)
  : Transform Outcome to Linear Predictor
- [`Generate_Beta()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/Generate_Beta.md)
  : Generate Sparse Coefficient Vector

## Estimation

Estimate the coefficients of a selected model.

- [`Beta_estimate()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/Beta_estimate.md)
  : Coefficient Estimation via Julia

## Julia setup

Connect R to Julia and install the Julia packages the package needs.

- [`setup_julia()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/setup_julia.md)
  : Initialize 'Julia' Environment
- [`install_julia_packages()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/install_julia_packages.md)
  : Install Required 'Julia' Packages
- [`install_julia_dependencies()`](https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/GICHighDimension/reference/install_julia_dependencies.md)
  : Install Julia and Required Packages
